chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Murram, from a man, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

"Whoever takes the scale with the intention of taking for himself a full measure will only take a surplus (more than due), and whoever gives with the intention of giving an equal measure will only give a deficient amount."
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of intention when weighing goods in trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on trade ethics, this hadith elucidates the metaphysical reciprocity of *niyyah* (intention) in commercial transactions. It teaches that a merchant who sincerely intends to give more than due will spiritually receive a surplus, whereas one who merely aims for exactness will receive a deficient measure, highlighting the spiritual weight of generosity in daily commerce.
